text: A train is stopped on the track. Behind it, another one is coming.
Its automatic train control has been switched off.
Sunday, November 8th. Fifty kilometres south of Cairo. Train 2010, Cairo to Aswan, stands between Kafr Ammar and Al-Raqqa.
On the same line, train 134 leaves El-Ayyat.
In the last coach of train 2010, passengers wait for it to move again.
Injured passengers said the train ran at high speed from the moment it left El-Ayyat station.
The two station staff admitted they did not monitor the control panel for signal tower 10.
Technical inspection confirmed the driver had switched off the automatic control system before the collision.
Seven people were killed. More than a hundred were injured.
The duty officer altered the signal log to cover up his negligence.
Both station staff are in custody.
The assistant driver is still too badly injured to be questioned.
Seventeen years ago, at the same place, another train ran into a stopped one. At least fifty people died.
